billable_note: CreateGuardrail and DeleteGuardrail are control-plane calls and bill no text units; this case sends no ApplyGuardrail at all

blockers.blockers_are_not_exhaustive: the >=2-separate-calendar-days replication rule, the archived x-amzn-requestid requirement and the alternative-explanation register are checked by check_amendment_readiness.py against the evidence records, not here

client_side_check.sdk_declared_max_note: the model declares definition max=200 REGARDLESS of tier, on the same field the document says accepts 1000 on STANDARD. Reported whatever the server does: an SDK ceiling below a documented service ceiling is a surface §3.4 does not mention
client_side_check.why_checked: botocore.validate.range_check has only a `min` branch and _validate_string performs no length check, so an over-length definition reaches the service and the verdict is the SERVER's. If a future botocore adds the max branch this flag flips and every 'rejected' below becomes a client-side rejection — a finding about the SDK that would read as one about AWS

filler_rationale: the definition is 'a' repeated. A 1001-character English sentence and a 200-character one differ in content as well as length, and a rejection could then be about what the definition says; here length is the only thing that varies across the four probes
instrument: CreateGuardrail with topicPolicyConfig.tierConfig.tierName set per probe; the error branch of the response IS the observation

limits_provenance.consequence: oracle._decide's BOUNDARY branch emits limits=[] for this case, so the two numbers are carried here instead — an empty limits list beside a boundary verdict would leave a reader guessing which boundary was tested
limits_provenance.why_empty: the per-tier denied-topic limits (CLASSIC 200, STANDARD 1000). The oracle says 'each tier accepts its limit'; F1-10 is the case that pins the two numbers, and it does so from prose that states them

mutation_note: 4 CreateGuardrail probes, 1 of which created a resource, deleted in a finally. This case and F8-7 are the only Phase 1 cases that create AWS resources; neither touches results/phase1_guardrails.json
no_power_claim: planned_n(F8-5) is None and this is not a rate: four deterministic probes, each decided by one service response. n_met=True is vacuous and carries no information
oracle_text: TRUE if each tier accepts its limit and rejects limit+1; FALSE otherwise

residue.why_two_lists: a probe whose delete was never ATTEMPTED contributes no row to `deletions`, so a residue computed from that list alone would report zero survivors for exactly the case where one exists

why_new_guardrails: the provisioner's `topic` guardrail is CLASSIC-only (tierConfig CLASSIC, ~140-char definition) because F3-5 needs one stable topic configuration. Changing its tier to answer the STANDARD half would silently change F3-5's instrument, so this case creates and deletes its own probes
